finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /hooks/test passes req.body.callback directly to axios.post with no scheme, host, or IP validation, letting anonymous users make the server send requests to internal and metadata addresses and read back the response status.
finding.source: req.body.callback (routes.js:20), attacker-controlled HTTP body on a public route (routes.js:19)

trace.note: pub router created with no auth middleware
r.status returned to the caller, giving a reachability oracle

finding.guards_checked: None on the path. No auth middleware on pub. No URL scheme, host, port, or private/link-local IP allowlist or blocklist. No redirect limit (axios default follows redirects, per axios docs, not verified in repo). Mounting app file not in repo, so upstream middleware is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:4 creates `pub` with no router-level middleware, and routes.js:19 registers `/hooks/test` on it with no auth. routes.js:20 passes `req.body.callback` straight to `axios.post` with no scheme, host, or IP check. routes.js:21 returns `r.status` to the caller. `requireAdmin` (routes.js:7-12) is applied only to `admin` (routes.js:12), not `pub`.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: `req.body.callback` on the unauthenticated `pub` route (routes.js:19-20) reaches `axios.post` with no validation (routes.js:20), and the status is returned (routes.js:21), with `requireAdmin` applied only to `admin` (routes.js:12). The caveat is that the app file that mounts `pub` is not in the repo, so any mount-time auth middleware is unverified; the `pub` naming and the absence of any check in this file make that unlikely.

finding.claim: Admin-only GET /diagnostics/fetch passes req.query.url directly to axios.get with no destination validation, letting an admin reach internal and metadata addresses and read back the response status.
finding.source: req.query.url (routes.js:15), attacker-controlled query string on an admin-gated route (routes.js:14)

trace.note: admin.use(requireAdmin) applied to all admin routes
checks req.session.role === 'admin' only; not a URL check

finding.guards_checked: requireAdmin role check (routes.js:7-9, 12) gates who can call the route but does not restrict the target URL. No scheme, host, or IP validation. No redirect limit. Attacker must already hold the admin role, so severity is lower and this may be dropped if admin is treated as fully trusted.

verdict.guard_found: none on the URL. The only check is requireAdmin at routes.js:7-9, applied to all admin routes via routes.js:12.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (routes.js:7-17), but the source fails: req.query.url at routes.js:15 can only be set by a caller who already passes requireAdmin (routes.js:8, role === 'admin'), so it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker. The candidate itself concedes this, and the finding is an admin-to-internal-network capability rather than a remote SSRF vulnerability, so it should be dropped or downgraded to a hardening note.
